title: Najdorf Variation (5...a6)
intro: The Najdorf stops White pieces from using b5. Meet 6.Be2 and 6.Be3 with ...e5, and answer 6.Bg5 or 6.Bc4 solidly with ...e6.
variation: e2e4 c7c5 g1f3 d7d6 d2d4 c5d4 f3d4 g8f6 b1c3 a7a6

lessons.title: Meeting 6.Be2 and 6.Be3
lessons.summary: Claim central space at once with 6...e5.

steps.text: Against the Classical 6.Be2, Black seizes central space and opens the f8 bishop.
Challenge the centre at once with the thematic Najdorf push.
steps.hint: Push the e-pawn two squares, chasing the d4 knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e5 to gain central space and drive the d4 knight back.
steps.ifRight: The knight must retreat, and Black develops ...Be7 and ...O-O smoothly.

steps.text: Develop your dark-squared bishop and prepare to castle.
steps.hint: Move the f8 bishop to e7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...Be7 so you can castle and play ...Be6.
steps.ifRight: Black will castle and place the light-squared bishop on e6.

steps.text: Against the English Attack (6.Be3), the same central strike works great.
Push the e-pawn two squares to kick the knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e5 to fight for d4 and open your dark-squared bishop.
steps.ifRight: After 7.Nb3, Black develops ...Be6 to guard d5.

steps.text: White stepped back to b3. Develop your light-squared bishop to challenge d5 and c4.
steps.hint: Put your c8 bishop on e6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...Be6 to control d5 and prepare ...Nbd7 and ...Rc8.
steps.ifRight: Black has a solid, active Najdorf set-up.

steps.text: 6.Bg5 is White's sharpest move, pinning the f6 knight and threatening Bxf6 or f4.
Break the pin cleanly and keep your pawn structure flexible.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e6: playing 6...e5 allows 7.Bxf6 followed by Nd5.

feedback.e7e5: After 6...e5 7.Bxf6 Qxf6 8.Nd5 Qd8, Black loses control of d5.

steps.text: White pushes 7.f4, threatening e5 or Qf3 and O-O-O.
Unpin your knight before White opens the centre.
steps.hint: Develop the f8 bishop to e7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...Be7 to unpin the f6 knight and prepare castling.
steps.ifRight: Now e5 is met safely and Black is ready for ...Qc7 and ...Nbd7.

steps.text: White brings the queen out with 8.Qf3 to prepare O-O-O.
Keep the c-file and e5 square under control while developing your queenside.
steps.hint: Move the queen to c7 so you can follow with ...Nbd7 and ...b5.
steps.ifRight: Black has a sturdy, counterattacking set-up against White's kingside.

lessons.title: Meeting 6.Bc4 and 6.h3
lessons.summary: Blunt 6.Bc4 with ...e6 and ...b5, and meet 6.h3 or 6.f3 with ...e5.

steps.text: With 6.Bc4, White targets the f7 and e6 squares right away.
Blunt the c4 bishop's diagonal immediately.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e6: this shuts down the c4 bishop and prepares ...b5.
steps.ifRight: Notice how the c4 bishop now hits a brick wall on e6.

feedback.e7e5: 6...e5 lets White control d5 while the c4 bishop still eyes f7.

steps.text: White retreats the bishop to safety with 7.Bb3.
Expand on the queenside with tempo against White's bishop and knight.
steps.hint: Push the b-pawn two squares to prepare ...Bb7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...b5 to gain queenside space and put your bishop on b7.

steps.text: Against 6.h3 (preparing g4), strike in the centre.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e5 (or 6...e6) to fight for the centre right away.
steps.ifRight: 6...e5 claims central space and meets g4 with ...Be6 and ...h6 or ...d5.

steps.text: Against 6.f3 (preparing Be3 and g4), play the classic central counter.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e5 to drive the knight back before developing ...Be6.
steps.ifRight: Black counters in the centre and prepares ...Be6 and ...Be7.
